nodes.label: COMPOSE_CMD
nodes.rationale: Mirrors scripts/asb's resolution of compose binary, per-host override and project name; previously hardcoded the `docker compose` plugin and the base file only, so every phase inspected containers that did not exist under the bot account (fixed 2026-09-14). `--profile full` is appended so hermes-v2/voice-gateway are visible to config/build/up.

nodes.label: sunday-upgrade-apply main sequence
nodes.rationale: EXIT trap kills only a recorded heartbeat pid (an unset pid made `kill 0` signal the whole process group and killed the test runner on 2026-09-24), drops both locks, and writes a FAIL handoff on any non-zero exit so prod never reads a stale PASS. Order: heartbeat, run lock, _record_head, pin capture from merge-base, phases, no-op gate (full runs only), cache prune, PASS handoff.

nodes.label: UPGRADE_LOCK
nodes.rationale: Advisory lock telling colima-health-check.sh a build is in flight so its socket-forward repair does not bounce the VM (2026-09-23 a repair killed an in-flight build). Re-stamped by the heartbeat and the build poll; lapses after AGENTSHROUD_UPGRADE_LOCK_MAX_AGE. Released immediately after builds finish because holding it defers the very socket repair the next step waits for (deadlocked a run on 2026-09-23). It is single-valued and advisory, never an exclusion mechanism; that is _take_apply_lock's job.

nodes.label: head-guard function extraction (line-number sed)
nodes.rationale: Extracts ONLY the real _record_head/_assert_head_unchanged definitions from sunday-upgrade-apply.sh and evals them (so the test fails if the real logic changes) rather than sourcing the whole script, whose top-level code parses argv and dies. Uses grep/sed line-number arithmetic instead of an awk range/exit pattern because some awk implementations buffer stdout and drop it on exit when piped, which silently produced an empty extraction during development. log/err are stubbed.

nodes.label: detects HEAD moving mid-run
nodes.rationale: Simulates the exact failure mode (another session commits/checks out on the SAME working tree) and requires _assert_head_unchanged to return failure with the specific message 'the working tree MOVED mid-run', not a generic error.

nodes.label: phase_apply build loop calls the guard every iteration
nodes.norm_label: phase_apply build loop calls the guard every iteration
nodes.rationale: Static check for the actual wiring: awk-extracts the `for svc in $build_list; do ... done` body of phase_apply and requires at least one _assert_head_unchanged call inside it, since the original single pre-loop call is unchanged and insufficient on its own (049cd5e051). Uses an awk range pattern, not exit, for the same buffering reason as the extraction.

nodes.label: no-baseline case returns success
nodes.rationale: With HEAD_AT_START empty (e.g. not a git repo at startup) the guard must never invent a failure; re-checks the documented early return.

nodes.label: _record_head captures real HEAD
nodes.rationale: In a throwaway git repo (REPO=TMP_REPO), _record_head must set HEAD_AT_START to rev-parse HEAD and _assert_head_unchanged must succeed while HEAD has not moved.

nodes.label: S15 asb _preserve_nonempty_secrets restores empty/missing values and keeps new non-empty ones
nodes.norm_label: s15 asb _preserve_nonempty_secrets restores empty/missing values and keeps new non-empty ones
nodes.rationale: Behavioral: evals the '# BEGIN/END preserve-nonempty-secrets' block from scripts/asb and runs _preserve_nonempty_secrets against two temp dirs; a 0-byte new copy and a missing new copy must be restored from the previous ephemeral secrets dir, while a non-empty new value must never be overwritten (expects 'old-url|old-key|new-pat').

nodes.label: Sunday apply exit-code contract
nodes.rationale: 0 all phases passed; 10 preflight/preconditions failed (nothing mutated, also used for a HEAD that moved mid-run); 20 scan gate; 25 NOTHING_UPGRADED although a newer upstream exists (mechanically green but achieved nothing); 30 apply failed, rollback attempted; 40 verify failed, rollback attempted; 50 rollback itself failed, human required; 127 required binary missing. The script is the deterministic core: the session proposes versions, this script disposes.

nodes.label: Prove the outcome, never the steps (CLAUDE.md 0.0)
nodes.norm_label: prove the outcome, never the steps (claude.md 0.0)
nodes.rationale: A no-op must be distinguishable from a success. Seven weeks of Sunday runs printed PASS while rebuilding the same OPENCLAW_VERSION; the fix is to assert on resulting state (pins changed, disk actually freed, container actually up) rather than on the exit code of the step that was supposed to change it.

nodes.label: Build one service at a time
nodes.norm_label: build one service at a time
nodes.rationale: `docker compose build` builds every service concurrently; the gateway image compiles cosign AND docker-cli from source, so parallel Go toolchains inside an 11GiB VM with zero swap OOM-killed the 2026-09-09 run after 26GB of layers. Sequential builds cap peak memory and make any failure attributable to a named service.

nodes.label: Shared working-tree stability guard
nodes.rationale: `docker compose build` bakes the working tree into the image, and this repo is checked out ONCE and shared. On 2026-09-24 a second session ran `git checkout` in the same directory during a live run; nothing crashed, the build would simply have shipped whatever was on disk at each COPY. Recording HEAD at startup and re-asserting it cannot make a shared checkout safe, but it turns a silent mis-build into a refusal. Extended 2026-10-04 (049cd5e051): gateway built one commit, the tree moved, openclaw built another, and the run's PASS did not notice, so the assertion now runs at the top of every per-service build-loop iteration, shrinking the blind window to one service's build time.

nodes.label: LLMProxy._failover_request
nodes.rationale: Cloud->local quota failover translates Anthropic/Gemini bodies to OpenAI shape for the local backend and back; if the local model also fails, falls back to OpenAI gpt-4o-mini using the gateway's own secret.

nodes.label: LLMProxy._forward_request
nodes.rationale: Retries 429/503/529 up to 3 times with Retry-After or exponential backoff; interactive callers (X-AgentShroud-Interactive: 1) skip retries so a 429 falls straight to quota failover. SCRUM-154: the whole urlopen+read+close runs on the executor thread so a stalled backend can't freeze the event loop.

nodes.label: LOCAL_MODEL_ROUTES
nodes.rationale: Model-name-prefix to backend base URL map; first-prefix-wins so more-specific IDs (gemma-4-26b-a4b-it, qwen3-14b-rapid, qwen3-coder, mlx-community/...) must precede generic entries (gemma, qwen3) or they would be shadowed and misrouted.

nodes.label: LLMProxy._normalize_local_model
nodes.rationale: LM Studio wants dashes, Ollama colons; Rapid-MLX only recognizes its weights by full local path (RAPID_MLX_MODEL_ID); oMLX's catalog ID for deepseek-r1-0528-qwen3-8b is DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B-6bit, so the documented alias 404'd on every call until corrected.

nodes.label: LLMProxy.proxy_messages (non-streaming)
nodes.rationale: Detects provider from path/model, rewrites Claude-via-OpenAI-path and Gemini-via-OpenAI-path requests with gateway-held keys, strips local provider prefixes, applies per-backend shims, then runs inbound scan -> forward -> OOM/secondary failover -> quota failover -> response translation -> outbound filtering + ToolACL.

nodes.label: LLMProxy.proxy_messages_streaming
nodes.rationale: Streams SSE chunks as they arrive via httpx (bypasses urllib buffering so OpenClaw's 60s fetch timeout does not fire). OpenClaw always sends stream:true so this path, not proxy_messages, is what real traffic hits; it must mirror prefix stripping, normalization and backend shims. with_head=True yields a StreamHead first; pre-header failures keep the in-stream SSE error frame contract.

nodes.label: LLMProxy._strip_fieldflare_unsupported_fields
nodes.rationale: Probed 2026-10-16: TurboFieldfare (:8238) answers 400 unsupported_value for parallel_tool_calls (any value), a named tool_choice object, and tool_choice 'required'; only 'auto'/'none' accepted. Hermes sends parallel_tool_calls with every tool-enabled request, so 9/9 dashboard turns on gemma-4-26b-a4b-it failed. Applied only when the resolved backend is FIELDFLARE_API_BASE, in both proxy paths, protecting any client on that route.

nodes.label: LLMProxy._suppress_qwen3_thinking
nodes.rationale: Qwen3 ignores chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking=false; only a '/no_think' text suffix disables chain-of-thought. 2026-10-16: Rapid-MLX's anchor is now Nemotron 3.5, which treated '/no_think' as literal user text (echoed into shell commands, tripped approval gate, 'typing forever'); non-Qwen models now get reasoning_effort: 'none' and untouched text.

nodes.label: LLMProxy._widen_optional_tool_param_types
nodes.rationale: Rapid-MLX's constrained tool-call decoding fills every optional argument with JSON null instead of omitting the key; widening non-required property types to accept null lets the harmless output pass validation without touching tool schemas.

nodes.label: Node ID format must match AST extractor
nodes.norm_label: node id format must match ast extractor
nodes.rationale: Semantic-extraction node IDs must use {immediate_parent_dir}_{filename_stem}_{entity}, exactly matching the AST extractor's ID scheme; using just the filename or the full path instead creates orphan 'ghost duplicate' nodes for the same entity, requiring `graphify extract --force` to rebuild cleanly.

nodes.label: Per-subfolder graphify-out avoids output clobbering
nodes.rationale: Running the skill pipeline on each monorepo subfolder separately would all write to the same graphify-out/ in the current working directory and clobber each other; using the CLI directly per subfolder places graphify-out/ inside the scanned path instead, avoiding the collision before a final merge-graphs step.

nodes.label: build_merge() avoids NetworkX round-trip (#801)
nodes.rationale: Incremental update uses build_merge() to read graph.json directly instead of round-tripping through NetworkX, because the round-trip was losing edge direction (calls/implements/imports) — tracked as bug #801.

nodes.label: Prune old nodes for changed files before AST re-insert (#1178)
nodes.norm_label: prune old nodes for changed files before ast re-insert (#1178)
nodes.rationale: Old nodes for re-extracted (changed) files must be pruned before inserting fresh AST results; otherwise the dedup pass tries to reconcile old and new versions of the same file's nodes and can collapse same-named symbols across different files — tracked as bug #1178.

nodes.label: Raw-flag triage discipline (74-merge sweep)
nodes.rationale: A 74-merge historical sweep of the repo showed most raw script flags were noise: generated/build files, 'good direction' flags where main's newer fix correctly overwrote a stale branch, or self-healed cases where a later commit already fixed the issue. Therefore no raw finding may be surfaced without passing the Check A/B/C triage (substantive change, ticket link, still-broken-at-HEAD) — otherwise the audit itself becomes a false-alarm generator.

nodes.label: LOCAL_PROVIDER_KEY mode-derivation design
nodes.rationale: LOCAL_PROVIDER_KEY is derived from AGENTSHROUD_MODEL_MODE rather than trusted from AGENTSHROUD_LOCAL_MODEL_REF's own prefix, because that ref can carry a stale/wrong provider prefix left over from a prior mode. Deriving LOCAL_MODEL_REF from the same LOCAL_PROVIDER_KEY keeps the primary model and the registered provider from ever diverging. Incident 2026-09-04: OpenClaw's primary model pointed at 'openai-local/<model>' while only 'ollama' was registered, causing every job to fail with FailoverError: Unknown model.

nodes.label: Telegram channel-wide fallback binding design
nodes.rationale: With multiple agents configured (main, per-collaborator, group-project/group-{chatId}), OpenClaw requires an explicit default owner for the Telegram account or it refuses to start the channel entirely, producing a crash-loop with growing backoff (observed 2026-09-15/16). `openclaw doctor --fix` can only auto-materialize this when every narrower binding names the same single agent, which is not the case here, so it must be set explicitly. The fallback binding falls through to 'main' for any sender not covered by a more specific peer/group binding; per-peer bindings always take precedence regardless of array order.

nodes.label: Telegram dmPolicy=open security tradeoff
nodes.rationale: dmPolicy='open' plus allowFrom=['*'] is required because OpenClaw's default 'pairing' mode drops messages without a prior /start handshake, which would prevent the gateway from delivering local command responses (/status, /approve) and collaborator-approval notices. The tradeoff — any Telegram user can initiate a conversation — is mitigated by the gateway's RBAC layer, which classifies owner/collaborator/stranger on every message before forwarding to the bot; unknown users receive only a pending-approval notice.

nodes.label: First-boot gateway-default s6 service auto-start
nodes.rationale: Vendor reconciler only auto-starts a profile whose last recorded state was running; a first-ever boot registers gateway-default but leaves its `down` sentinel, so the container reports healthy while the Telegram gateway never runs (43+ hours observed 2026-07-19). Removing the sentinel and s6-svc -u fixes it; idempotent on later boots.

nodes.label: MCP servers reconciliation from mcp/servers.json into config.yaml
nodes.norm_label: mcp servers reconciliation from mcp/servers.json into config.yaml
nodes.rationale: Writes mcp_servers: in config.yaml directly instead of `hermes mcp add` because that CLI is discovery-first and interactive (prompts get EOF under s6 init and crash-looped the container). Must actively DISABLE entries marked enabled:false in servers.json, not just add — purely additive reconciliation left a stale agentshroud-gateway entry enabled for weeks (~213 failed connections/day, 2026-08-01).

nodes.label: Env-split cron reconciliation (AGENTSHROUD_PROD_CRON_KEEP)
nodes.rationale: Owner directive 2026-08-29: dev resumes every Hermes cron job so local-model output can be iterated; prod pauses everything except the pipe-separated AGENTSHROUD_PROD_CRON_KEEP keep-list. Runs last so it covers seeded and live-created jobs. Must invoke hermes via /opt/hermes/.venv/bin/python3 because `hermes` is not on PATH (silent no-op bug found 2026-09-04). Writes marker /opt/data/.agentshroud-prod-cron-keep-empty and a stderr banner when the keep-list is empty on prod, because the 2026-10-12 recreation paused all 35 jobs (incl. Daily Brief) with only an INFO line.

nodes.label: Tirith trust seeding (lookalike_tld + internal gateway HTTP rule)
nodes.norm_label: tirith trust seeding (lookalike_tld + internal gateway http rule)
nodes.rationale: Hermes's tirith URL scanner blocks .ai/.security/.dev/.io competitor domains under lookalike_tld, filling competitive reports with UNVERIFIED markers; scope-only-to-rule trust entries narrow the bypass. Gateway host trusted only for the plain-HTTP-in-exec rule, discovered at runtime from `tirith explain --list` so a renamed rule can't silently no-op. The `|| true` guard is load-bearing: calling the nonexistent `tirith rules list` under set -euo pipefail aborted the whole script and took the container down every 25-40s (crash storm 2026-07-20).

nodes.label: Missing-secret visibility banner (expected secrets loop)
nodes.rationale: Checks every expected secret from inside the container and folds missing ones into the Telegram 'Hermes online' banner, because run-standalone.sh's silent WARN-and-skip let Feedbin credentials go missing for two days. Since 2026-10-16 an upper-cased env var of the same name counts as present (feedbin_* are passed as env vars, so every prod boot had falsely flagged them). Also surfaces the init-config.sh prod-cron-keep-empty marker in the same message.

nodes.label: S1 start-agentshroud.sh launches openclaw with --stack-size=65536
nodes.rationale: ARM64 V8 stack overflow fix: the openclaw node launch must carry --stack-size=65536 or the bot crashes on arm64 hosts (2026-04-10 session bug).

nodes.label: S2 apply-patches.js sets channels.telegram.apiRoot
nodes.rationale: Telegram photo download through the proxy requires channels.telegram.apiRoot to be assigned in apply-patches.js; without it photo fetches bypass the proxy and fail.

nodes.label: Auto-start a stopped Colima VM (step 1a)
nodes.rationale: Cron is the only autostart that works on this host: a RunAtLoad LaunchAgent bootstraps into the Aqua domain at GUI login and the agentshroud-bot account never gets one (all dev work arrives over SSH), and its /tmp log paths collide with admin's agent. Gated on the dev account so a VM is never booted on prod. timeout 300 bounds a hung start under the 15-min stale-lock window.

nodes.label: Daily summary state tracking
nodes.rationale: Accumulates heal/fail/docker-down counts in /tmp JSON state and sends at most one Telegram summary per 24h to avoid notification spam.

nodes.label: Colima VM default-route auto-heal (step 2)
nodes.rationale: Colima's DHCP client assigns eth0 an address but does not always install a default route. colima ssh is key-based with passwordless sudo, so this IS fixable from cron (an earlier comment claimed otherwise). Probes via $GATEWAY_CONTAINER, not a literal name that does not exist on this host.

nodes.label: Container net-diag expected-failure baseline (step 5)
nodes.rationale: 8 expected failures (re-derived 2026-09-20), every one a consequence of egress enforcement via HTTP(S)_PROXY=gateway:8181. The count is COMPARED against AGENTSHROUD_DIAG_EXPECTED_FAILS, not just logged — the prior branch reported ANY number as expected, the fake-green pattern CLAUDE.md section 2 prohibits. docker exec failure sets 99 so it surfaces.

nodes.label: DOCKER-USER iptables reapply + verify (step 3)
nodes.rationale: DOCKER-USER chain lives on the VM, not in the cap_drop:ALL gateway container. Both rule counts must run under sudo: without it iptables errors and grep -c reads 0, so the firewall was reapplied every 5 minutes and reported 0/5 after printing 5 healthy rules. A recheck after reapply prevents counting a heal that did nothing (inflated to ~265/day on 2026-08-30).

nodes.label: Dead docker.sock forward repair (step 1a-bis)
nodes.rationale: lima establishes the docker.sock forward exactly once at VM start; when the ssh connection drops, colima ssh/status keep working while every docker call fails (four times on 2026-09-21). Bouncing the VM is the only reliable repair. Done as bounded stop (300s) THEN bounded start (420s) rather than one `colima restart`, because the single-command form blew its budget, was killed mid-flight, and only recovered by accident via step 1a a tick later. 300+420=720s stays under the 900s stale-lock threshold to avoid two racing colima starts. Deferred while _upgrade_in_progress.

nodes.label: colima-vm-flags behavioral check (2026-10-16)
nodes.rationale: Runs the real _colima_vm_flags block: with a saved colima.yaml it must yield only --network-address; without one the explicit --cpu/--memory/--disk defaults; and the LaunchAgent plist must carry no sizing flags.

nodes.label: Strip comments before grepping for regressions
nodes.norm_label: strip comments before grepping for regressions
nodes.rationale: Scripts under test DOCUMENT the old behaviour at length in comments, so a naive grep matches the prose and reports a regression that is not there (happened on first run for the llm_settings installer, the colima restart, and the colima start count). Checks therefore sed-strip comments first, or execute the real function instead of grepping.

nodes.norm_label: s10 start-agentshroud.sh force-reconciles security-critical live cron jobs
nodes.rationale: The init-openclaw-config.sh cron reseed is a whole-file checksum gate that only touches the seed file on disk; OpenClaw's live cron store is sqlite-backed and existing job IDs are left alone. Positive-presence check for _reconcile_security_critical_cron, _SECURITY_CRITICAL_CRON_JOB_IDS and 'openclaw cron edit' in start-agentshroud.sh.

nodes.norm_label: s11 init-openclaw-config.sh seeds jira_dev_ticket.py into live openclaw workspace

nodes.norm_label: s12 hermes init-config.sh seeds jira_dev_ticket.py into live hermes workspace

nodes.label: S8 no raw ssh/agentshroud-bot@/real Tailscale FQDN in baked bot config
nodes.norm_label: s8 no raw ssh/agentshroud-bot@/real tailscale fqdn in baked bot config
nodes.rationale: Bots run sandboxed with no LAN route and no Tailscale daemon; the only lab-host path is agentshroud-ssh-exec.sh via gateway /ssh/exec. PRs #313/#314/#315 each patched a single file and left sibling copies (docker/bots/openclaw/config/cron/jobs.json, workspace/SOUL.md) instructing raw ssh. Repo-wide negative grep over openclaw/hermes config dirs using three precise signals (ssh <host> command, agentshroud-bot@ user@host, tail<hex>.ts.net FQDN) with one literal exception for the git author identity agentshroud-bot@agentshroud.ai; deliberately no surrounding-phrase exclusion because a prior version whitelisted the bug text.

nodes.label: S9 init-openclaw-config.sh seeds agentshroud-ssh-exec.sh rules into live AGENTS.md
nodes.norm_label: s9 init-openclaw-config.sh seeds agentshroud-ssh-exec.sh rules into live agents.md
nodes.rationale: Positive-presence check (S8 is negative-only). Local models (Qwen3, qwen2.5-coder, deepseek-r1) reliably obey only the live workspace AGENTS.md, not SOUL.md; a freshly scaffolded AGENTS.md with no SSH-exec rule let a failed-over local model try raw ssh/ping with zero guidance (2026-07-29). Requires AGENTS_FILE and agentshroud-ssh-exec.sh in the init script.

nodes.label: start.sh (Hermes s6 main program / startup wrapper)
nodes.norm_label: start.sh (hermes s6 main program / startup wrapper)
nodes.rationale: Does NOT launch its own `hermes gateway run`: the vendored image's s6-rc gateway-default service already does, and a second instance raced it for the Telegram getUpdates session, lost the Conflict, died, and (being s6's main program) took the whole container down in a restart loop. This script only stays alive so the TERM/INT trap (Telegram lock release + shutdown notice) fires.

nodes.label: _release_telegram_lock
nodes.rationale: Calls Telegram Bot API `close` plus a getUpdates offset=-1 drain before shutdown so the restarted instance does not hit 'Conflict: terminated by other getUpdates' (20s x 5 backoff).

nodes.label: _telegram_send
nodes.rationale: All Telegram traffic routes through the gateway's /telegram-api reverse proxy, never direct to api.telegram.org; X-AgentShroud-System: 1 marks system notifications so the gateway skips outbound content filtering.

nodes.label: Crash backoff escalation (rolling 10-minute start window)
nodes.rationale: More than 5 starts in 600s pauses 300s before proceeding, to prevent runaway Telegram rate-limiting during asyncio crash-loops and let the getUpdates long-poll lock expire on Telegram's side. Sends a Telegram notice first so the owner knows why Hermes goes quiet.

nodes.label: Post-migration model lock + sandboxed terminal + cron fleet default
nodes.norm_label: post-migration model lock + sandboxed terminal + cron fleet default
nodes.rationale: Hermes schema migration resets model.default to a cloud model on every fresh volume; resolve_model.py decides model+provider from the container env after /health comes up. terminal.* keys must be set via `hermes config set` (env vars only reach an internal probe). cron.model/cron.model_provider is a separate resolution axis from model.default — left unset, every cron job blocked with 'No Anthropic credentials found' (2026-08-14).

nodes.label: asb build
nodes.rationale: The only subcommand allowed to call `$COMPOSE build --no-cache` without the profile flag (test_bot_boot_static S16 permits at most one bare build call).

nodes.label: asb clean-rebuild [full|hermes]
nodes.rationale: Interactive-confirmed variant of rebuild that also removes the gateway-data and clamav-db volumes. hermes-config is never deleted because it persists Hermes skills, cron, MCP and memory. Same profile-flag-to-build fix as rebuild.

nodes.label: COMPOSE (asb compose command string)
nodes.rationale: Built on CE from detect_container_runtime; for the agentshroud-bot account it adds the per-host override docker/docker-compose.agentshroud-bot.<host>.yml and -p PROJECT so dev and prod stacks on one host are distinct. setup_ephemeral_secrets later appends the generated secrets override to it.

nodes.label: asb down
nodes.rationale: Uses --profile full so voice-gateway is stopped too; Hermes is stopped via run-standalone.sh; the ephemeral secrets dir is removed to rotate secrets.

nodes.label: _PROFILE_FLAG
nodes.rationale: Set to '--profile voice' when the 'full' argument is given. Must reach `compose build` as well as `compose up`: without it compose builds only un-profiled services, so `asb rebuild full` brought every container up on fresh images EXCEPT voice-gateway, which silently kept its old image (prod 2026-10-16 rebuild from a7b8cee1e2; fixed in bd0c1225bd).

nodes.label: PROJECT (compose project name)
nodes.rationale: 'agentshroud' for prod, 'agentshroud-bot' for the bot account; exported so docker-compose.yml's ${PROJECT} interpolation can tell containers their compose-project-prefixed network names (OpenClaw sandbox.docker.network).

nodes.label: asb rebuild [full|hermes]
nodes.rationale: Full teardown, prune, fresh secrets, `$COMPOSE $_PROFILE_FLAG build --no-cache` (profile flag passed to build since bd0c1225bd so voice-gateway is rebuilt under 'full'), optional hermes build, sandbox image check, up, device-store reset, post-deploy check.

nodes.label: asb up [full|hermes]
nodes.rationale: 'full' maps to --profile voice plus a standalone Hermes launch; 'hermes' launches only Hermes standalone. Runs post-deploy-check.sh and a prune on every bring-up.

nodes.label: S16 asb rebuild/clean-rebuild build with $_PROFILE_FLAG
nodes.rationale: Without --profile voice, compose build only builds un-profiled services, so 'asb rebuild full' left voice-gateway on its old image (prod, 2026-10-16). Requires >=2 '$COMPOSE $_PROFILE_FLAG build --no-cache' lines in scripts/asb and at most 1 bare '$COMPOSE build --no-cache' (only the plain build command may be bare).

nodes.label: Compose profile gating (voice/hermes/full)
nodes.rationale: voice-gateway and hermes are behind compose profiles and are invisible to `config`/`build`/`up` without an explicit --profile flag. Every compose invocation that is supposed to touch them must carry the flag, otherwise the profiled service silently stays on its old image while the run reports success. asb uses `--profile voice` for 'full'; sunday-upgrade-apply.sh appends `--profile full` to COMPOSE_CMD for the same reason (fixed there 2026-09-14).

nodes.label: No Security Theater (Rule A-E)
nodes.rationale: AgentShroud is a security product; stubs, placeholders, skip markers, and hardcoded mock data ship vulnerabilities behind green checkmarks. Requires explicit STUB labeling with a failing test when something can't be fully implemented, file:line citations for every codebase claim, and a five-line integration proof (entry point/routing/handler/test/evidence) before anything is called 'integrated'.

nodes.label: Prove the Outcome, Never the Steps
nodes.norm_label: prove the outcome, never the steps
nodes.rationale: Written after four mechanisms (scan gate, CVE auto-registration alert, Sunday upgrade, dev-to-prod handoff) each reported PASS/success while doing nothing real. Mandates asserting on resulting state (before/after deltas) rather than exit codes, giving no-ops a distinct status/exit code, and never claiming an action in user-facing text the code doesn't perform.

nodes.label: Weekly Upgrades: EVERYTHING Means Everything
nodes.rationale: Owner directive 2026-09-01/09-15: every versioned component (wrapped agents, security sidecars, containers, dependencies, gateway code, vendored code, host tooling) goes to latest stable every Sunday, determined mechanically not from memory, with two independent remediation arms per CVE (vendor patch + AgentShroud's own gateway-level attack-class mitigation) so third-party agents that never receive the vendor fix are still protected.

nodes.label: Rule: agentshroud-hardcoded-password

nodes.label: Rule: agentshroud-log-sensitive-key
nodes.rationale: Logger calls passing token/password/secret/key-named variables risk sensitive data exposure in logs (CWE-532).

nodes.label: Rule: agentshroud-pickle-load
nodes.rationale: pickle.load/loads on untrusted data enables insecure deserialization (CWE-502); use json or Pydantic instead.

nodes.label: Rule: agentshroud-sql-injection
nodes.rationale: String-formatted SQL queries (%, .format, f-strings) risk SQL injection (CWE-89); require parameterized queries.

nodes.label: Rule: agentshroud-ssrf-httpx
nodes.rationale: httpx calls with dynamic URLs risk SSRF (CWE-918) unless validated against the egress allowlist.

nodes.label: Rule: agentshroud-ssrf-requests
nodes.rationale: requests calls with potentially user-controlled URLs risk SSRF (CWE-918).

nodes.label: Rule: agentshroud-subprocess-shell-true
nodes.rationale: Blocks subprocess calls with shell=True — enables shell injection (CWE-78) if any argument is user-controlled.

nodes.label: Rule: agentshroud-subprocess-unvalidated-input
nodes.rationale: Warns when subprocess args may include unvalidated user-controlled values (CWE-78).

nodes.label: Root cause: Nemotron in-band reasoning + Qwen-only /no_think suffix
nodes.norm_label: root cause: nemotron in-band reasoning + qwen-only /no_think suffix
nodes.rationale: The 2026-10-11/12 Sunday upgrade swapped Rapid-MLX's anchor model from qwen3 to Nemotron 3.5. Nemotron reasons in plain text and exhausted max_tokens (finish_reason=length), and the gateway's _suppress_qwen3_thinking appended /no_think keyed on backend URL not model, which Nemotron treated as literal text — Hermes echoed it into a shell command that tripped the elevated-command approval gate. Fixed by --default-reasoning-effort none in local-llms and by gating /no_think to models containing 'qwen' with reasoning_effort:none for others (commit 0ffa0cd794).
